- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–4 days; if sentiment shows strong reversal signal (e.g., 0.5+ then drops), adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; cap first 5–7 days’ forecast at 10–15% below recent 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4), model exhibits erratic behavior; use sentiment median as smoothing filter for 3–5 day forecast adjustments.
